name: Tomato and Tomatillo Salad

ingredients.name: mixed ripe tomatoes, cut into bite-size pieces
freshly ground black pepper, plus more for serving
ball of burrata, room temperature, torn into large chunks

instructions.primary_message: Place chopped tomatoes and tomatillos in a colander set over a large bowl and season with 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt. Toss to coat. Set aside at room temperature to drain, tossing occasionally until tomatoes release their juices, a minimum of 15 minutes and up to 1 hour.
Discard juice from bowl and transfer tomatoes to now-empty large bowl.

In a separate bowl, combine shallots and vinegar, and let sit for 5 minutes, stirring halfway through. Pour shallots through a fine-mesh strainer set over a medium bowl (don't discard vinegar). Transfer shallots to large bowl with tomatoes and set aside.
Add agave or honey, oregano, mustard, garlic, pepper, and remaining 3/4 teaspoon salt to bowl with vinegar; whisk until combined. Slowly whisk in olive oil until smooth and emulsified.
Add 1/4 cup of vinaigrette to bowl with tomatoes and shallots; toss to combine. Transfer to serving bowl or platter.
Top with burrata, almonds, and basil. Drizzle remaining vinaigrette evenly over salad. Finish with freshly ground pepper and flaky sea salt, if desired. Serve immediately.

schema_metadata.keywords: tomato salad, tomato salad recipe, tomato and tomatillo salad, summer salad recipe

description: Juicy tomatoes, tangy raw tomatillos, and creamy burrata team up in this bright, summery salad with a punchy white balsamic dressing. It comes together easily with a few simple prep tricks.
notes:
Optional or for serving: Flaky sea salt, such as Maldon, for sprinkling (optional)

Optional substitutions: agave nectar → honey

Notes: This salad is meant to celebrate peak tomato season and won't be nearly as good if made with out-of-season tomatoes. Any ripe tomatoes will work in this salad.
Tomatillos have a sticky layer underneath their husks. To remove this layer, firmly rub tomatillos under running water after removing their husks.

Make-ahead and storage: The vinaigrette can be made in advance and stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 1 week. Whisk or shake well in a tightly sealed jar before use.
The salad is best when eaten right away, but it can be stored at room temperature for up to 1 hour or refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 1 day before serving. If refrigerating, bring to room temperature before serving and drain any excess liquid that has pooled.
author: Laila Ibrahim
